the energy consumption in WSNs is not only a result of the hardware and software, but also a consequence of the network architecture and the network topology.
the power sources of wireless sensor networks can be categorized into three groups: energy harvesting, energy storage and battery.
the power consumption for the sensor network is a complex problem and it is not a single factor that determines the power consumption of a wireless sensor network.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the energy consumption of a sensor network is mainly due to the communication between sensors and base stations.
we have developed an algorithm for a wireless sensor network that uses a hybrid energy model to optimize the network lifetime.

the energy consumption sources for WSNs can be classified into three categories: the energy consumption sources from sensor nodes themselves, the energy consumption sources due to the communication between sensor nodes, and the energy consumption sources caused by the environment.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the power consumption of the wireless communication module in a sensor node dominates the overall energy consumption.
energy consumption in WSNs can be reduced by 50% or more by simply reducing the amount of data transmitted by the nodes.
energy consumption is not a major concern for WSN applications that are not battery constrained.
